text:
maya: Quick heads up — ran the KV cache long-run smoke regtest against main after yesterday's kernel layout change. Summary below.

eng-ci: CI run finished: kvcache-longrun-smoke — FAILURE. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/1754129876 (logs + heap profiles)

sam: What failed? OOM or assertion?

eng-ci: OOM on worker-3 at ~1.9M tokens. Container OOM killed process. See /artifacts/worker-3/oom.log

qa-bot: regression detected: mem_growth_slope increased by 2.3x vs baseline (longrun suite). Eviction throughput down ~3x.

maya: Reproduced locally on my devbox with --tokens=2000000. Memory climbed steadily, fragmentation spikes ~1.6G before OOM.

eli: Any change in eviction heuristics or page size from the kernel change?

maya: The kernel packing change switched from pad-based layout to compressed packing and adjusted page alignment. Suspect fragmentation: many small free blocks but no contiguous region for reuse.

rhea: Do we have perf counters? Can we get compaction stats per epoch?

maya: Sample compaction output attached:
```
[compaction] epoch=42 freed_bytes=1.2M fragments=128 reused_blocks=14
[kv] total_alloc=12.8G live=11.3G fragments=1.6G
```
Fragment count spikes line up with the layout merge.

sam: Interesting — reuse rate dropped from ~65% to ~12% after the patch. That explains the steady mem growth.

eli: FYI kernel selector change: we picked block-aligned kernels for better throughput; it looks like that forced different KV page sizes. I'm starting a bisect.

eng-ci: Bisect job kicked off: sh ./eng/runtime/test_tools/kvcache_bisect.sh --base=main~5 --head=main. Will post results.

qa-bot: Synthetic workload details: interleaved prefix-reuse pattern (A,B,A,B...), sequence lengths 1024/4096, bursty short tails to force eviction and reuse churn.

maya: Repro steps added to the harness:
```
./tools/run_kvcache_longrun --model=rwkv-lite --tokens=2000000 --pattern=interleave --trace-kvcache
```
Trace flag dumps free-list events and coalescing attempts.

rhea: Can we add a CI regression asserting reuse_rate >= 50% for pattern=interleave? If it falls below, fail the job and flag the change.

eli: I'm prototyping a compaction micro-pass that coalesces adjacent free blocks during low-load windows. Local tests show reuse improves to ~58%.

sam: Nice. Any p95 latency impact?

eli: Micro-pass is async + bounded; synthetic bench shows ~0.4% p95 increase but memory stabilizes. Tradeoff looks acceptable for Dedicated workloads.

maya: Proposed plan:
1) Land compaction pass behind feature flag.
2) Add regression test to CI (reuse_rate threshold + mem_slope checks).
3) Finish bisect to identify minimal kernel commit that changed packing.
4) Add auto-fallback in Dedicated to previous packing if mem growth detected.

sam: +1. Also add an observability metric: "kvcache.coalesce_failures" and alert when >100/min.

rhea: I'll open an RFC "kvcache-packing-compaction" and attach benchmark graphs, traces, and the proposed flag.

maya: Trace snippet (from --trace-kvcache):
```
free_event: time=1234 id=0x7fabc size=256 coalesced=false
alloc_event: time=1235 id=0x7fdef size=1024 owner=worker-3
coalesce_attempt: time=1240 left=0x7fab right=0x7fb0 merged=false reason=alignment_mismatch
```
Looks like alignment prevented coalescing in many cases.

eng-ci: Next CI run (with compaction feature flag on) scheduled in ~30m; tagging @eli @sam @rhea for visibility.

eli: Will watch the run and follow up with bisect output.

sam: thx everyone — please add short repro notes to the PR so QA can run nightly longruns. :thumbsup:   

maya: Thanks — I'll open the PR with flag + tests and link the RFC.
